messages:
PagerDuty Bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: prod-gpu - queue growth detected (90th pct queue time > 45s), autoscaler errors seen. AlertID: PD-984322. Pager: @Carla (oncall)
InfraBot: auto-scaling event failing: lastScaleError: "allocation throttled: hit globalScaleLimit=12". Current GPU nodes: 12, Requested pending pods: 48.
Carla (oncall): On it. What region/pool?
Ben K.: prod-gpu in us-west2, mix of A100 80G and A100-40G MIG slices. Most pending pods request 1g.
Alice M.: seeing binpack failures in scheduler: logs: 
```
I0221 14:07:12.345 kube-scheduler summary: NoNodesAvailable: 48 nodes didn't match node selector
error: allocation failed: insufficient allocatable gpus; fragmentation: available slices found but size mismatch
```

Dave R.: autoscaler logs show repeated throttles from allocator: 
```
ERROR allocator: scale request denied: reason=GlobalScaleLimitReached limit=12
WARN allocator: retrying in 30s
```

Eve S.: Customer impact: Support queue has 6 tickets from customers reporting slow responses; a few large customers seeing 500s on inference calls. Latency dashboard: tail P95 token latency spiking to 6s, request rate steady.
Frank C.: btw large embed batch jobs started ramping at 13:58 which coincides with queue growth. Could be a runaway background job.
Carla (oncall): plan: 1) determine whether we can temporarily relax globalScaleLimit for prod to allow emergency scale-up 2) if not, manual mitigation: evict lower-priority pods, repack nodes, or switch some traffic to fallback model variants. Who can run the limiter check?
Ben K.: I can run check. Running `rkctl allocator status --pool prod-gpu --json` now.
Ben K.: result: {"globalScaleLimit": "12", "currentActiveScale": "12", "queuedScaleRequests": "4", "maxNodesAllowedByQuota": "12"} — quota is the blocker.
Alice M.: Quota = customer quota from cloud account? Looks like we've hit committed capacity for the Dedicated cluster. If we increase quota, it will take time. We need short-term steps.
Dave R.: short-term: 1) identify reclaimable pods (non-prod, low-priority) 2) trigger immediate preemptible evictions 3) fallback routing to smaller models. I can run a repack command to binpack smaller slices to free contiguous MIG groups.
Carla (oncall): execute evict list, but coordinate with support so we don't kill a paying customer. Eve, can you enumerate tickets and map to instance ids?
Eve S.: pulling mapping. 3 of the 6 tickets are from orgs on dedicated capacity (they shouldn't be evicted). 2 are from non-prod test accounts, 1 is internal load test.
Frank C.: Suggestion: reduce MIG slice sizes for new allocations (switch requests to 1g slices from 2g) and enable packing policy to avoid fragmentation. That requires runtime config push.
Ben K.: I can toggle packing policy: `rkctl runtime update --pool prod-gpu --packing=aggressive` — will push in ~30s. Doing it now.
InfraBot: packing policy update accepted. New policy effective in 38s.
Alice M.: meanwhile I'll trigger a targeted eviction of non-prod pods: `kubectl get pods -l env!=prod -n inference -o name | xargs kubectl delete --grace-period=0 --force` (will run with caution). Ready to run on your mark.
Carla (oncall): Wait. Pause. We must avoid deleting anything in orgs with reserved capacity. Eve, confirm which namespaces are safe.
Eve S.: Safe namespaces: staging-*, loadtest-*. Not safe: redwood-corp-prod, acme-inc-prod.
Carla (oncall): Ben, finish packing toggle. Alice, run selective delete only for staging/loadtest. Dave, start repack job. I'll coordinate comms.
Ben K.: packing toggle done. InfraBot: cluster reported improved matching: scheduler re-evaluating pending pods.
Dave R.: kicking off `repack-controller --pool prod-gpu --strategy compact-mig --dry-run=false` — this will try to co-locate slices to free full-size allocations. Estimated time 4-6 minutes.
InfraBot: repack job started, job_id=rp-202602. Progress: scanning nodes (0/240 scanned).
Carla (oncall): I've paged the ACME contact (Frank C.) and Sales ops. Sending note to customers on affected SLIs. Eve, add that to support ticket PD-984322.
Frank C.: on it. Patch message: "We are actively remediating a capacity issue affecting inference latency for a subset of requests. We're executing capacity repack and targeted evictions. ETA 10-20m for stabilization."
Alice M.: ran selective evictions for staging/loadtest. Freed 8 pods worth of GPU. Scheduler now scheduling ~12 pending pods onto reclaimed slices.
Ben K.: autoscaler still reports limit reached but currentActiveScale remained 12. But packing improvements reduce fragmentation; pending pods reduced from 48 to 10 in 3 mins.
InfraBot: repack progress 240/240 nodes scanned, 92 migrations executed, reclaimed 3.6 full GPUs worth of capacity.
Dave R.: I've also temporarily bumped fallback routing via the traffic router to send 20% of heavy requests to `model-sm` (smaller, cheaper variant) to reduce load. Will monitor error rates.
Eve S.: support update posted. Some customers confirm improved throughput. One large customer still seeing errors — looks like their traffic hit a single hot node prior to repack.
Carla (oncall): If this stabilizes, we keep monitoring and open a ramp plan for quota increase and a postmortem to adjust default MIG sizing and autoscaler limits. If not stable in 15m, escalate to execs.
Ben K.: Pending queue now 2, p95 latency returning toward normal. Autoscaler shows queuedScaleRequests drained.
InfraBot: alert PD-984322 condition cleared at 14:22:30.
Carla (oncall): Good job. Quick retro notes here: 1) autoscaler globalScaleLimit should surface quota origin in alert 2) packing policy default too conservative for 1g workloads 3) add a safety override for oncall to temporarily increase scale limits subject to guardrails.
Alice M.: I'll file the postmortem ticket and add action items: investigate default MIG sizing, improve non-prod isolation to avoid noisy neighbors, and create a runbook for reclaim/packing fast path.
Frank C.: I'll follow up with customer ops & sales for impacted accounts and track any revenue risk.
Ben K.: leaving handoff to night oncall, Carla to escalate if anything recurs. :thumbsup:
Carla (oncall): Handoff to night oncall @Ben (night). I'll update incident channel and close once 1h stable. Thanks all. :eyes:
